Kolkata will become the 18th city connected to the Water Metro network.

recent_articles.title: Sixty next-generation trains to be introduced for Kolkata Metro in 5 years: Vaishnaw - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw** announced plans to introduce 60 next-generation trains for the Kolkata Metro over the next five years, aiming to revitalize railway projects in West Bengal. **Vaishnaw**, who visited the state secretariat Nabanna with **Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari**, highlighted the progress made since 2014, including the addition of 45 km of metro lines. He also discussed proposed bullet train services between Delhi–Varanasi and Varanasi–Siliguri, which aim to reduce travel time significantly.

recent_articles.title: Kolkata to get water metro, will be the 18th city to be linked, says CM Adhikari | Kolkata News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, the Chief Minister of West Bengal, announced plans to separate the shipping sector from the transport department and develop minor ports similar to those in Gujarat and Odisha. He also stated that Kolkata will become the 18th city connected to the Water Metro network. **Adhikari** highlighted efforts to improve marine infrastructure, including a deep-sea project at Dadanpatrabar, and plans for the Gangasagar Mela to be an international event. Additionally, he proposed establishing a museum at Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port to showcase the history of old Kolkata.

recent_articles.title: "Can Send Her To Assembly": Expelled Leader's 'Offer' For Mamata Banerjee
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Humayun Kabir**, a former Trinamool Congress leader who formed his own party, Aam Janata Unnayan Party (AJUP), has offered to give **Mamata Banerjee** an assembly seat in Murshidabad if she requests it.  Kabir won two seats in the recent election and now claims he can ensure her victory from Rejinagar by resigning. **Banerjee**, who lost her Bhabanipur seat, must win a by-election to return to the state assembly.

recent_articles.title: Plague On Both Your Houses: Bengal Minister On Divided Trinamool
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Swapan Dasgupta**, a senior Bengal BJP leader, advised against supporting **Trinamool Congress** rebels, stating that the people's mandate for a "complete detoxification process" should be allowed to unfold. He believes the BJP should not intervene in the internal divisions within the party and instead focus on fulfilling its mandate of providing good governance to West Bengal. Dasgupta criticized both factions of the **Trinamool Congress**, suggesting that neither is deserving of support, as they are plagued by corruption and lack of integrity.

recent_articles.title: Ritabrata Banerjee, Mamata Banerjee Anatomy Of A Loss: Inside The Collapse And Rise Of "Real Trinamool"
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Following the Bengal election loss, **Mamata Banerjee**, a three-time chief minister, faces growing dissent within her party.  **Ritabrata Banerjee**, a Trinamool MLA, and other dissidents have publicly challenged **Abhishek Banerjee**, Mamata's nephew, accusing him of centralizing power. The rebellion escalated when the dissidents were expelled from the party and formed their own leadership team. They now claim to represent the "real Trinamool Congress" in the Assembly, while seeking guidance from **Mamata Banerjee**.  The situation has led to a power struggle within the party as it attempts to regain control.

recent_articles.title: Who Is Firhad Hakim, Close Mamata Banerjee Aide Who Quit As Kolkata Mayor
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mamata Banerjee** faced a major split within her **Trinamool Congress**, with 59 of 80 MLAs supporting rebel leader Ritabrata Banerjee.  The party also saw the resignation of Firhad Hakim as Kolkata Mayor after around 100 councillors deserted the party.  Hakim had previously offered his resignation but was initially refused by **Mamata Banerjee**. Senior Trinamool leader Kunal Ghosh confirmed that Hakim's decision to resign was made with dignity and that **Mamata Banerjee** eventually agreed to it. The split comes after an administrative meeting at the state secretariat Nabanna, where several Trinamool MLAs attended, including Hakim.

recent_articles.title: Mamata Banerjee, Abhishek Banerjee, Leader of Opposition, Ritabrata Banerjee, Sandipan Saha - "Real" Trinamool Backs Rebel For Key Post, Says 'Mamata Banerjee Our Leader'
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Trinamool Congress** MLA Ritabrata Banerjee claims to have the support of 59 MLAs, aiming to challenge **Mamata Banerjee's** nominee for Leader of Opposition, **Sobhandeb Chattopadhyay**.  Banerjee alleges forged signatures on a letter supporting Chattopadhyay. The Assembly Secretariat has filed a police case into the matter, with the CID investigating. Chief Minister **Suvendu Adhikari** stated that three Trinamool MLAs confessed to not signing the document.

recent_articles.title: Trinamool dissolves party units after rebels’ defiance show, says will introspect | Kolkata News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Trinamool Congress** leadership has dissolved all party committees and frontal organizations following the defiance of 60 of its 80 MLAs in the West Bengal Assembly. The party will undertake a comprehensive review and assessment before reconstituting its organizational structure.  This move comes after a series of events, including the expulsion of two MLAs for allegedly forging signatures on a communication endorsing Sovandeb Chattopadhyay as Leader of the Opposition. This rebellion has shaken the leadership, with some loyalists remaining steadfast while others have challenged the party's direction.

recent_articles.title: From Shakhas to Cabinet: The RSS Loyalists in Camp Suvendu Adhikari | Kolkata News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The newly sworn-in **BJP** cabinet in West Bengal features a number of leaders who rose through the ranks of the **Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS)**.  These individuals, including Tapas Roy, Dudh Kumar Mondal, Gouri Shankar Ghosh, Dipak Barman, Dr Ajay Poddar, Dr Sharadwat Mukherjee, Manoj Kumar Oraon, Arup Kumar Das, and Malati Rava Roy, have a history of working within the party's grassroots organization.  Roy, Mondal, Ghosh, Barman, Poddar, Mukherjee, Oraon, Das, and Roy all previously held positions in local bodies or as MLAs before joining the cabinet.

recent_articles.title: Ex-House Help Kalita Majhi Takes Oath As Bengal Minister Of State
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kalita Majhi**, a BJP MLA from Ausgram, was sworn in as Minister of State on Monday.  She joined **Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari**'s cabinet, expanding the West Bengal Council of Ministers to 41.  Majhi previously worked as domestic help and had to give up formal education due to financial hardship. She began her political career as a booth-level worker and was elected in the 2021 Assembly elections.

recent_articles.title: Bengal Cabinet Expansion: Meet 35 New Faces In Suvendu Adhikari's Government
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari** expanded his **West Bengal** government on Monday, inducting 35 ministers. The expansion includes 13 Cabinet Ministers, three Ministers of State (Independent Charge), and 19 Ministers of State, reflecting the BJP's commitment to regional, social, and community representation.  The new cabinet members represent a mix of experienced legislators, former parliamentarians, professionals, and first-time ministers. This move is seen as an effort to strengthen governance while accommodating diverse perspectives across the state.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal Cabinet Expansion Live Updates: WB CM Suvendu Adhikari Cabinet Ministers Expansion 2026 Portfolio Wise Minister Oath Ceremony Latest Updates
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, the Chief Minister of West Bengal, is set to expand his council of ministers today with 35 BJP MLAs taking the oath. The expansion will bring the total number of ministers in the state cabinet to 41, exceeding the constitutional limit by three positions.  The new ministers represent various communities and regions, including North Bengal, women, tribals, and Matuas. **Amit Malviya**, a senior BJP leader, is among those expected to join the ministry. The expansion aims to solidify the party's support base after its victory in the recent state elections.

recent_articles.title: TMC MLAs, Abhishek Banerjee attack: Only 20 attend Mamata Banerjee Kalighat meeting - India Today
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **TMC** General Secretary **Abhishek Banerjee** was attacked on Saturday, leading to a low turnout at a legislative party meeting called by **Mamata Banerjee**. Only 20 of the 80 newly elected MLAs attended the meeting at her residence. The absence of nearly three-fourths of the legislators raised concerns, but **TMC** spokesperson **Kunal Ghosh** stated that many were protesting against alleged political violence and police action against party workers.  The party announced plans for protests in rural areas and urban wards on Monday, followed by a sit-in led by **Mamata Banerjee** at Rani Rashmoni Road on Tuesday.

recent_articles.title: Bengal Cabinet expansion today, 35 new ministers to be sworn-in - India Today
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, the **West Bengal** Chief Minister, will oversee a cabinet expansion on Monday with at least 35 new ministers to be sworn in. The ceremony, scheduled for 11 am at Lok Bhavan, will be attended by Governor RN Ravi and Prime Minister Narendra Modi.  Prominent BJP leaders expected to join the ministry include former TMC strongman **Arjun Singh**, cricketer-turned-politician **Ashok Dinda**, former Rajya Sabha MP **Swapan Dasgupta**, and actor **Rupa Ganguly**.

recent_articles.title: 35 Ministers To Take Oath In West Bengal Cabinet Expansion Tomorrow
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, West Bengal's new chief minister, announced that 35 ministers will be sworn in on Monday. The swearing-in ceremony will take place at 11 am at Lok Bhavan and will be administered by **Governor RN Ravi**. This expansion of the cabinet brings the total number of ministers to a full council for the nationalist government elected by the people of West Bengal.

recent_articles.title: June 1 New Rule Changes: LPG Cylinder Rates, PAN Update, Advance Tax Deadline and CBSE Guidelines
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE)** will open the re-evaluation process for Class 12 students from June 1, while **Southern Railway** has revised schedules for over 200 suburban train services on the Chennai Beach–Tambaram–Chengalpattu corridor.  **Commercial flight services** are scheduled to begin at Noida International Airport in Jewar on June 15, becoming the second international airport serving the Delhi-NCR region. **The Indian government** is implementing new rules requiring the use of domestically manufactured solar cells for all net-metering and open-access projects commissioned after June 1.  These changes affect various sectors including transportation, energy, education, and welfare programs.

recent_articles.title: Opposition praises EC for peaceful Bengal Assembly polls | BJP, Congress praise Election Commission for ‘by and large peaceful’ first phase of Bengal Assembly polls so far - Telegraph India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Opposition leaders** and prominent political figures, including **Suvendu Adhikari**, **Dilip Ghosh**, **Mausam Benazir Noor**, and **Udayan Guha**, cast their votes in the first phase of the Bengal Assembly election.  Sporadic incidents of violence were reported during polling, but overall security arrangements appeared to be effective. The state recorded an average voter turnout of 41.11% in the first four hours of voting.  The Election Commission has been praised for its efforts in conducting the polls peacefully.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal Cabinet expansion on June 1 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, the West Bengal Chief Minister, is expected to expand his Cabinet on June 1st and allocate key portfolios to senior **BJP** leaders. The first **BJP** Cabinet in the state will likely have over 30 members, with names announced after approval from the party's central leadership.  The selection criteria for the new ministers will consider seniority, regional representation, and experience, aiming to ensure inclusion of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, women, and representatives from northern and south western Bengal. The Cabinet expansion follows **Adhikari**'s recent swearing-in as a Minister and his oversight of 42 state departments.

recent_articles.title: Census in West Bengal to start from August 1: CM Suvendu - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, West Bengal Chief Minister, announced the commencement of the **West Bengal Census 2027** between August 1 and February 2028. He emphasized that the census is a constitutional obligation and urged citizens to participate.  Adhikari attributed demographic changes in parts of the state to cross-border infiltration due to an unfenced border with Bangladesh, stating that accurate data will be crucial for governance and planning. The **Census Director of West Bengal**, Rashmi Kamal, IAS officer of the 2006 batch, is overseeing the digital census, which allows for self-enumeration.

recent_articles.title: No legal action if infiltrators go back on their own: Amit Shah - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Amit Shah**, **Union Home Minister**, announced the formation of a high-level committee to address demographic change and commit to deporting all infiltrators from the country. He stated that those who voluntarily return would not face legal action, citing an increase in voluntary returns since the BJP came to power in West Bengal.  **Suvendu Adhikari**, **West Bengal Chief Minister**, fulfilled a promise of providing land for border fencing within 45 days of his government's formation and handed over 600 hectares of land to the Border Security Force (BSF).

recent_articles.title: Trinamool MLA arrested, several leaders quit party post - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Dilip Mondal**, a Trinamool Congress MLA from Bishnupur, was arrested by **West Bengal police** in Odisha on Wednesday (May 27, 2026) after days of evading arrest. The arrest follows an investigation into alleged threats against **BJP** workers during the West Bengal Assembly elections and a previous complaint filed against him.  The arrest marks the first time a sitting MLA has been apprehended by **West Bengal police**. This comes amidst a wave of arrests targeting local Trinamool Congress workers, including former Minister **Sujit Bose**, for their alleged involvement in corruption and post-poll violence. The situation is further complicated by mass resignations from Trinamool leaders, including senior leader **Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar** and several councillors.  The party's leadership is also facing criticism for the lack of a designated space for the Leader of Opposition, **Sovandeb Chattopadhyay**, in the West Bengal Assembly premises.

recent_articles.title: Suvendu urges BJP workers to follow law, says government will do ‘sabka hisab’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, West Bengal Chief Minister, announced that his administration will implement a policy of "Sabka Hisab" (holding everyone accountable), alongside the existing slogan "Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas" (everyone's support, everyone's progress). This initiative is aimed at the **Trinamool Congress** leadership, which has governed West Bengal for the past 15 years.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal gained infamy due to recruitment scams, new recruitment policy in next Budget session: CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, West Bengal Chief Minister, announced a new recruitment policy for the state during the Rojgar Mela in Sealdah. The policy will be introduced in the next Budget session of the assembly, beginning on June 18th.  Adhikari cited previous recruitment scams under the Trinamool Congress regime, including teacher and municipal job scandals, as reasons for the new policy. He also expressed concerns about the lack of transparency in examinations and suggested a carbon copy of the OMR sheet be given to all examinees to prevent nepotism and corruption.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal government to detect, delete and deport illegal infiltrators, says CM Adhikari - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, West Bengal Chief Minister, announced a new policy of "detect, delete, and deport" for illegal infiltrators.  He stated that the state police will arrest those not covered under the Citizenship (Amendment) Act and hand them over to the **Border Security Force (BSF)** for deportation. The announcement was made during an event where land was handed over to the BSF for border fencing along 27 km of the India-Bangladesh border.  The Chief Minister also emphasized the revival of district-level coordination mechanisms between the BSF, state police, and administration in bordering areas.

recent_articles.title: Adhikari aide killing: CBI conducts searches at multiple locations - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The CBI** conducted searches at multiple locations in connection with the murder of West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari's aide Chandrakant Rath. The agency took over the investigation from the **West Bengal Police**, forming a seven-member special investigation team under a DIG of Special Crime from Delhi.  Rath was shot dead on May 6th, two days after the West Bengal Assembly election results were declared. Three individuals have been arrested in connection with the case, while police believe at least eight people were involved.

recent_articles.title: BJP MLA Rathindra Bose to be party's candidate for Speaker's post - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Bharatiya Janata Party** in West Bengal has nominated **Rathindra Bose**, a first-time MLA and chartered accountant, as its candidate for the Speaker of the West Bengal Legislative Assembly.  Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari urged opposition parties to unanimously elect him. The elections are scheduled for May 15, 2026.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal government mandates singing Vande Mataram in all State-run schools during morning assembly - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, West Bengal Chief Minister, issued an order mandating the singing of **Vande Mataram** in all state-run schools during school assembly prayers. This order overrides a previous directive requiring schools to sing the state song, **Banglar Mati, Banglar Jol**. The move comes amidst political tensions surrounding the national song's recognition and follows a BJP campaign highlighting alleged neglect by the Trinamool Congress government.

recent_articles.title: ED arrests Kolkata Police DC Shantanu Sinha Biswas in money laundering case - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Enforcement Directorate (ED)** officials arrested **Shantanu Sinha Biswas**, Deputy Commissioner of Kolkata Police, on Thursday for his alleged involvement in land grabbing and money laundering linked to businessman **Sona Pappu**.  The arrest follows repeated summons by the ED and a lookout notice issued against him for failing to appear. The investigation is ongoing, with the ED seeking information from the West Bengal Police regarding Biswas' current deployment. This marks the second high-profile arrest by the ED since the change of regime in West Bengal.

recent_articles.title: Priorities and Challenges before Suvendu Adhikari government in WB - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Following a decisive victory in the 2026 West Bengal Assembly elections, the **BJP** government faces significant challenges. The priority is to create employment opportunities, attract industries, and maintain law and order within the state.  The success of these initiatives will be crucial for the party's continued governance.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal CM gives sanction to CBI to prosecute officials in several scams - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, West Bengal Chief Minister, granted permission to the **CBI** to prosecute officials involved in teacher's recruitment, municipality recruitment, and cooperative scams.  He stated that these investigations were previously withheld by the previous Trinamool Congress government due to corruption concerns. The move is part of a "zero tolerance" policy against corruption adopted by his BJP-led administration.  The Chief Minister also lifted a ban on potato sales to other states, citing a bumper crop and falling prices.

recent_articles.title: BJP MLA Tapas Roy sworn in as Pro-tem Speaker of West Bengal Assembly - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tapas Roy**, a senior Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader and MLA from Maniktala, was sworn in as the Pro-Tem Speaker of the West Bengal Assembly on Tuesday, May 12, 2026. **Suvendu Adhikari**, the Chief Minister, attended the ceremony. The oath-taking of other MLAs will be held on Wednesday and Thursday, with the election for Speaker scheduled for Friday.

recent_articles.title: Suvendu Adhikari to chair first Cabinet meeting on May 11, 2026 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, the newly elected Chief Minister of **West Bengal**, will hold his first cabinet meeting on Monday, May 11, at Nabanna.  The meeting will see the allocation of portfolios to five ministers who were sworn in with him on Saturday. The cabinet is expected to establish inquiry commissions into atrocities against women during the **Trinamool Congress** regime. Adhikari also plans to meet with top officials from various departments including the police and district magistrates.

recent_articles.title: WB CM Suvendu Adhikari to chair first cabinet meeting today - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, the newly elected Chief Minister of West Bengal, will hold his first cabinet meeting on Monday (May 11, 2026) at Nabanna. The meeting is expected to allocate portfolios to five ministers who were sworn in alongside him on Saturday (May 9). **Adhikari** also plans to establish inquiry commissions into atrocities against women during the previous Trinamool Congress regime and meet with top officials of various departments including police, district magistrates, and the Director General of West Bengal police.

recent_articles.title: Regional, caste calculus in BJP’s West Bengal Cabinet choices - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** appointed five ministers in West Bengal, including **Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari**, to reflect regional and community considerations.  **Dilip Ghosh**, **Agnimitra Paul**, **Ashok Kirtania**, **Kshudiram Tudu**, and **Nisith Pramanik** were sworn in on Saturday (May 9, 2026), representing diverse regions and caste backgrounds. The appointments aim for a balanced representation within the state's legislature.  The BJP now holds a majority in the West Bengal Assembly after winning 207 seats.

recent_articles.title: Fresh overhaul in Suvendu Adhikari administration likely in near future, say officials - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The newly installed **Suvendu Adhikari**-led BJP government in West Bengal is undertaking a sweeping recalibration of its administrative structure, following the unprecedented scale of pre-poll reshuffle by the Election Commission of India.  **Subrata Gupta**, a retired IAS officer who served as Special Roll Observer during the ECI's exercise, was appointed Advisor to the CM, while **Shantanu Bala**, an Additional District Magistrate, was appointed Private Secretary to the CM. The government also reassigned at least 46 WBCS (Executive) officers and transferred 16 officers from the Chief Minister’s Office, signaling a broader realignment of power corridors in Bengal's bureaucracy.  These changes are seen as part of a larger effort to reshape the state apparatus under the new BJP dispensation.

recent_articles.title: Suvendu Adhikari | The Bengal pivot - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, a prominent Trinamool Congress leader, defected to the **BJP** in December 2020 after several senior party members attempted to persuade him to stay.  Adhikari's decision was driven by his ambition to become West Bengal's Chief Minister, an aspiration he felt unattainable within the **Trinamool Congress**. His departure came as a significant blow to the party, especially with the emergence of **Abhishek Banerjee**, Mamata Banerjee's nephew, who had gained prominence in the political landscape.

recent_articles.title: Sheikh Hasina, Awami League congratulate Suvendu Adhikari - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sheikh Hasina**, former Prime Minister of Bangladesh, congratulated **Suvendu Adhikari**, the new Chief Minister of West Bengal.  The **Bangladesh Awami League**, banned in Bangladesh, expressed support for Mr. Adhikari and stated that they believe this new chapter will elevate relations between Bangladesh and India. The Awami League was banned following a crackdown on civilians in 2024.

recent_articles.title: People celebrate with sweets and colour as ‘Kanthi’s son’ takes oath in Bengal - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kanthi**, the hometown of **Suvendu Adhikari**, celebrated his swearing-in as West Bengal's Chief Minister on Saturday.  His father, **Sisir Adhikari**, a veteran politician, expressed pride in his son's achievement and thanked the people for choosing him. He urged his son to serve the state wholeheartedly and focus on its development.

recent_articles.title: Naidu and Pawan congratulate Suvendu Adhikari on taking oath as West Bengal CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **N. Chandrababu Naidu**, **Prime Narendra Modi**, and **K. Pawan Kalyan**  attended the swearing-in ceremony of **Suvendu Adhikari** as Chief Minister of West Bengal in Kolkata. **Naidu** congratulated the new government and expressed his best wishes for its success, while **Pawan Kalyan** highlighted the significance of the BJP's victory in addressing concerns about violence, lawlessness, and national security.

recent_articles.title: Which party governs which State/UT: In maps - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** and its allies secured victories in Assam, Puducherry, and West Bengal, while the Congress-led UDF won in Tamil Nadu. **Suvendu Adhikari**, a BJP leader, is set to become the first BJP Chief Minister of West Bengal. The results mark a shift in the political landscape with the BJP or the NDA now governing 20 states and 2 Union Territories.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal Cabinet 2026: From Dilip Ghosh to Agnimitra Paul, Ministers who were sworn in along with Suvendu Adhikari - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, newly sworn in as the Chief Minister of West Bengal, inducted five new ministers into his cabinet on Saturday. The swearing-in ceremony was attended by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, **Union Ministers Amit Shah, Rajnath Singh, J. P. Nadda, and Dharmendra Pradhan**, among other BJP leaders.  **Dilip Ghosh**, a senior BJP leader who secured victory in the Kharagpur seat, **Agnimitra Paul**, a fashion designer-turned-legislator who won Asansol Dakshin, **Ashok Kirtania**, a BJP stalwart who gained victory in Bangaon Uttar, and **Kshudiram Tudu**, a former school teacher from Ranibandh (ST) constituency, were among the newly appointed ministers.  **Nisith Pramanik**, a key face of BJP from North Bengal, was also inducted into the cabinet.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal oath-taking LIVE: Suvendu Adhikari sworn in as first BJP CM of West Bengal, five other MLAs also take oath - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, the newly sworn-in BJP Chief Minister of West Bengal, was inaugurated by Governor R.N. Ravi alongside five other MLAs who will join his cabinet. The ceremony was attended by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and senior members of the NDA, including ministers from the Central Government and other state chief ministers.  Post-election violence has erupted in the state since the results were announced on May 4th, with Adhikari's personal assistant being shot dead on May 6th.

recent_articles.title: Suvendu Adhikari to become the first BJP Chief Minister of West Bengal - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari** was unanimously elected leader of the Bharatiya Janata Party's legislature party in West Bengal following their victory in the recent assembly elections. **Amit Shah**, Union Home Minister, presided over the meeting and supported **Adhikari's** nomination.  The BJP secured 207 seats, while the Trinamool Congress won 80.  **Adhikari** then met with Governor R.N. Ravi to formally stake his claim to form a government.

recent_articles.title: ​Take east: On the BJP government in West Bengal - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** secured a resounding victory in the West Bengal Assembly elections, winning 207 out of 294 seats.  **Suvendu Adhikari**, former Leader of the Opposition and now the new Chief Minister, defeated incumbent **Mamata Banerjee** in her own constituency, marking a significant shift in power dynamics. The BJP's success can be attributed to its strategic focus on booth-level organization, leveraging Hindu identity politics, and exploiting popular dissatisfaction with the TMC's governance.  The party's victory comes with challenges, including restoring law and order after targeted violence.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal government formation LIVE: Amit Shah arrives in Kolkata for BJP legislature party meet to elect new CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The BJP legislature party** will meet in Kolkata on Friday, May 8, 2026, to elect its leader with **Suvendu Adhikari** emerging as the frontrunner.  Following the BJP's historic victory in the West Bengal Assembly elections, ending the **TMC’s** 15-year rule, **Mamata Banerjee**, the current Chief Minister, has refused to resign and accused the verdict of being a result of a conspiracy. Post-election violence has also erupted across the state since the election results were announced on May 4, 2026, with **Suvendu Adhikari’s** personal assistant being shot dead by unidentified gunmen on Wednesday, May 6, 2026.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal Governor dissolves State Legislative Assembly - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **R. N. Ravi**, the Governor of West Bengal, dissolved the state's Legislative Assembly on May 7, 2026, ending the 17th assembly term. The move follows the BJP's victory in the recent assembly elections, securing a majority and leading to the end of **Mamata Banerjee**'s Trinamool Congress rule.  The swearing-in ceremony for the new BJP government is scheduled for Saturday, May 9, 2026, at the Brigade Parade Grounds.

recent_articles.title: Suvendu Adhikari aide killing: Driver undergoes multiple surgeries, still critical - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chandranath Rath**, a close aide of **Suvendu Adhikari**, the BJP leader, was shot and killed in North 24 Parganas on Wednesday night.  The driver of Rath's car, **Buddhadeb Bera**, sustained bullet injuries and underwent multiple surgeries. His condition remains critical. The incident has sparked outrage, protests, and renewed allegations of political violence in West Bengal following the state elections.

recent_articles.title: Tension grips parts of North 24 Parganas after murder of Suvendu’s aide; security tightened - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tension** prevailed in parts of West Bengal's North 24 Parganas district following the shooting death of **Chandranath Rath**, a close aide of BJP leader **Suvendu Adhikari**.  Police deployed additional forces in Madhyamgram, Doharia and surrounding areas after **BJP** supporters protested for the immediate arrest of the assailants. The incident has been described as a "targeted assassination" by the **BJP**, while the **TMC** denies any involvement. Police are conducting raids and examining CCTV footage to identify the perpetrators.
